body: Another thought: If I read RFC 8259 correctly the default encoding for `application/json` should (must) be UTF-8 if no specific charset is specified: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8259#section-8.1

issue.title: Non-English Character Handling Issue in the Request Tab (like Korean)

repository.name: zaproxy
repository.description: The ZAP by Checkmarx Core project

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

Hi ZAP :D
I'm having an issue with handling Korean in ZAP's Request tab.
I think it would be an encoding/decoding problem for non-English speaking countries. 
> Both Korean(`e.g 한글`) and Japanese(`e.g ひらがな`) are replaced by the same (`???`)

## When I send it
- When there is Korean in the URL Query: It results in an error.
- When there is Korean in the Header: It's processed correctly.
- When there is Korean in the Body: It's processed correctly, but it's displayed as `???`.

https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/assets/13212227/b9d58a12-40e4-4d63-ab30-40315add5602

## When I read it
When viewing Req/Res in the History tab, Korean text is displayed as `???` in Req under specific conditions, regardless of whether it's in Form or JSON. (I don't know the conditions 😭)

**Normal case (httpie to zaproxy)**
![](https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/assets/13212227/22ae8035-4519-4010-8275-6edb352c7f33)

**Broken text case (mobile app to X)**
Original
```json
{"message": "ㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋ"}
```

to ZAP
```json
{"message" : "ããããããããã"}
```
![](https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/assets/13212227/75ba2d2b-3367-49ab-8fc6-bb780804692b)


to Caido
```json
{"message": "ㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋ"}
```

![](https://github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/assets/13212227/11737d53-7b85-4ad7-8c8d-ae3b0a4a9d32)


### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `Open Manual Request Editor`
2. Send this
```
POST https://www.hahwul.com?query= HTTP/1.1
host: www.hahwul.com
header: 한글

body=한글
```

### Expected behavior

- I'd like Korean to be displayed correctly in the Request tab, just like in the Response tab.
- Instead of URL Query error, encoding like `%ED%95%9C%EA%B8%80` is likely to be required.
